decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm elbow-up approach; key is on right and slightly farther forward than reference. Left remains parked.
Continue raising elbow and pitching right gripper toward downward grasp, with smooth forward arc.
Approach above the visible key while continuing elbow-up wrist pitch; keep gripper open.
Finish downward approach toward key neck, compensating the observed forward shift. Check wrist alignment before closing.
Fine-align right fingers with the key neck from wrist view; compensate lateral offset and in-plane angle before grasp.
Center fingers just above the bow at the key neck, then close right gripper without moving the key laterally.
Allow closure to settle and begin a small vertical test lift; verify key retention visually.
Key appears retained at the neck; lift it clear of the table by more than five centimeters, keeping the right gripper closed.
Retained key is clear of the table. Bring right hand toward the shared handover boundary and rotate key shaft toward the right, exposing its bow to the left hand.
Continue right-hand presentation with key retained. Begin lifting left elbow smoothly in its own workspace to prepare for bow grasp.
Bring right presentation nearer center while left follows an elbow-up arc toward horizontal receiving orientation; both remain on their own sides.
Finish right handover presentation and advance left receiver along a raised-elbow arc. Maintain closed right grip and separation.
Hold the presented key steady while left receiver advances and rotates toward the exposed bow, retaining elbow-up configuration.
Finish receiving orientation and approach the bow from the left, slowing before final contact; right maintains retention.
Continuity guard stopped the last step; replan from observed pose with smaller receiving-wrist increments and partial opening.
Advance left fingertips toward the exposed key bow, keeping partial opening and right-hand hold; monitor alignment before closing.
Seat the exposed bow between left fingertips with a slow final approach. Keep right hand fixed and closed until left grip is established.
Bow has reached left fingertips with some contact-induced tilt; stop translation and close left gradually while right keeps supporting the key.
Bow is visibly below left finger center and tilting under contact. Keep right retention; reopen and back left off slightly, lowering receiver before retry.
Use the exposed bow in left wrist view to correct receiving position while right continues holding. Small forward and height adjustments only.
Center exposed bow in the receiving jaws and make a short final advance; start gentle left closure while right remains stationary and closed.
Close left jaws around the now-centered bow without translating either arm. Keep right support through closure.
Left closure did not clearly capture the bow. Maintain right retention and reopen left for a small deeper, slightly higher receiving approach.
Bow is visibly centered deeper in the left jaws. Close left without further translation and keep right supporting.
Left fingers closed without clear retention. Keep right holding and correct receiving depth and bow-center offset by a few millimeters before retrying.
Close left around the bow at the deeper position, holding both wrists fixed and keeping right grip until retention is visually assessed.
Bow is between left jaws. Test handover by gradually opening right while left stays closed and both wrists remain fixed; check for falling or slipping.
Key shifted during right release; retention is uncertain. Keep left closed and clear right fingers slowly to inspect whether left holds or key has slipped.
Key slipped to table. Retract left receiver and reacquire with right, orienting to its new diagonal shaft while descending with clearance.
Continue right reacquisition toward key neck and finish diagonal alignment. Keep left clear of the downward approach.
Shift right grasp forward along the key axis and lower toward neck height. Use wrist view for the remaining alignment; left stays clear.
Fine-center the key neck in right wrist view and finish descent to grasp height; left remains safely retracted.
Correct the neck offset along its axis at fixed height before reacquiring. The key is still on the tabletop.
Bring the visible neck back to the right fingers' grasp region, then begin closure. Avoid further descent into the table.
Close the right gripper on the centered neck and begin a small test lift; verify retention before the next handover attempt.
Lift the reacquired key clear with right gripper closed and begin returning its shaft to a horizontal handover direction; verify that it remains between the fingers.
Key is retained. Raise it for another handover and gradually level the key plane, presenting the bow toward the left receiver.
Level both handover frames: right presents a flat key along +X and left approaches along +X with vertical jaw closure, staying clear until alignment is checked.
Approach the flat bow with corrected receiver height and lateral alignment; keep left jaws open and stop short for visual confirmation.
Bow remains lower than receiving finger center in the side view. Lower left slightly and advance slowly to place the flat bow between vertical-closing jaws.
Contact tilted the key and its bow is still below the left grasp center. Reopen, back off, and lower the receiving jaws while preserving right retention.
Key slipped during contact. Clear the left hand and reacquire farther along the key shaft with right, leaving more bow exposed for transfer.
Continue right approach, aligning to the new key angle and keeping ample shaft exposure for a later bow grasp. Left waits clear.
Approach farther along the shaft rather than at the bow, finishing in-plane alignment and descent. This should leave more space for left-hand capture.
Center the shaft, not the bow, in the right fingers and close at tabletop grasp height. The longer exposed bow should permit a separated handover.
Let right closure settle around the upper shaft and test a short lift, checking that the bow remains attached below the grip.
Continue a straight test lift with right closed; assess retention of the upper-shaft grasp before moving toward handover.
The key remained on the table. Reopen and return toward the neck rather than the extreme tip, descending to the prior grasp height.
Align the neck with right jaw center and close; its bow is now visibly behind the grasp region, with no further tabletop descent.
Settle right closure at the neck and make a short vertical lift to confirm retention before another transfer.
Key is visibly retained at the neck. Lift and present toward the left while keeping clear of the receiving fingers.
Raise retained key to handover height and rotate its shaft toward the receiver. Left remains open and clear pending visual bow alignment.
Finish right presentation while correcting left receiving height before contact, using the exposed bow in the left wrist image as the alignment cue.
Bow is now centered across the left jaws in wrist view. Advance horizontally without changing height, leaving right hand fixed and closed.
Fine-center the bow by raising left slightly during the last short advance. Keep the right supporting grip unchanged.
The bow is centered between left fingertips in the wrist image. Close the receiving gripper without moving either wrist, retaining right support.
Left jaws visibly contact the bow. Keep left closed and wrists fixed while gradually releasing right for handover verification.
The bow remains seated in left jaws after right release. Clear right horizontally while left holds still, confirming the handover before reorientation.
Handover is visually retained. Clear right farther and begin left elbow-up reorientation of the key toward upright insertion, with the bow clamped.
Raise and rotate the retained key in a continuous elbow-up arc toward vertical, keeping right arm parked clear.
Continue smooth left wrist reorientation and lift, retaining the bow. Approach vertical without moving either arm across the workspace boundary.
